behaviour: q = 3329, zetas = 17^bitrev7(i) mod q. The forward transform is FIPS 203 algorithm 9; the inverse is algorithm 10 including the final multiplication of every coefficient by 3303. The transform replaces the 256 coefficients in place (natural order in and out as in the algorithms).
BUSY is high for at most 1200 clocks per transform (reference 896 forward, 1152 inverse); CYCLES reports the count. No divide or remainder operators.
Loads are accepted only while idle. The coefficient pair p is words {c[2p+1], c[2p]}; LD_PTR and RD_PTR count pairs 0..127.
LED[0] = DONE, LED[1] = BUSY, the other LEDs are 0.

"""Acceptance tests of c16_ntt_engine against model.py (hidden from the agent)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import cocotb
from benchmark.lib.bench import Board, peek
from model import (CYCLES, DESIGN_ID, LD_DATA, LD_PTR, RD_DATA, RD_PTR, START_FWD, START_INV, STATUS, bench_cases,
                   intt, ntt)


async def transform(b: Board, name: str, op: str, poly: list[int]) -> None:
    await b.write(LD_PTR, 0)
    for p in range(128):
        await b.write(LD_DATA, poly[2 * p] | poly[2 * p + 1] << 16)
    await b.write(START_INV if op == "inverse" else START_FWD, 1)
    await b.cycles(1250)
    await b.expect(STATUS, 2, f"{name}: DONE and not BUSY")
    cyc = await b.read(CYCLES)
    assert 100 <= cyc <= 1200, f"{name}: BUSY for {cyc} clocks (must be at most 1200)"
    want = (intt if op == "inverse" else ntt)(poly)
    await b.write(RD_PTR, 0)
    for p in range(128):
        got = await b.read(RD_DATA)
        w = want[2 * p] | want[2 * p + 1] << 16
        assert got == w, f"{name}: {op} coefficients {2 * p},{2 * p + 1}: RTL 0x{got:08X}, model 0x{w:08X}"


@cocotb.test()
async def test_identity_and_reset(dut):
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    assert await b.shell_id() == DESIGN_ID
    for off in (LD_PTR, RD_PTR, STATUS, CYCLES):
        await b.expect(off, 0, f"reset value of {off}")


@cocotb.test()
async def test_forward_random(dut):
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    await transform(b, *bench_cases()[2])


@cocotb.test()
async def test_inverse_random(dut):
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    await transform(b, *bench_cases()[3])


@cocotb.test()
async def test_forward_edge_polynomials(dut):
    """A single one (the transform is all ones) and all coefficients 3328 (the largest values)."""
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    for c in bench_cases()[:2]:
        await transform(b, *c)


@cocotb.test()
async def test_registers_and_reset(dut):
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    await b.write(LD_PTR, 5)
    await b.write(LD_DATA, 0x0123_0456)
    await b.expect(LD_PTR, 6, "LD_PTR advances per write")
    await b.write(RD_PTR, 5)
    await b.expect(RD_DATA, 0x0123_0456, "pair 5 reads back")
    await b.expect(RD_PTR, 6, "RD_PTR advances per read")
    await b.write(STATUS, 3)
    await b.expect(STATUS, 0, "STATUS is read-only")
    for off in (0x08, 0x41, 0x7F):
        await b.expect(off, 0, "unmapped")
    led = await peek(b.clk, dut.LED)
    assert led == 0, f"LED {led:04X}: idle, nothing done"
    await b.reset()
    await b.expect(LD_PTR, 0, "LD_PTR after reset")

spec_md:
# NTT engine behind the test shell

I want a block for the Nexys A7-100T's FPGA that computes the "number-theoretic transform" used in the post-quantum key-exchange standard FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), forwards and backwards, on a polynomial of 256 coefficients, and I want to exercise it entirely from the test shell.

- Every coefficient is a whole number from 0 to 3328 (arithmetic is modulo q = 3329). The transform is exactly the one in FIPS 203: "NTT" is algorithm 9 and "NTT inverse" is algorithm 10, including the final multiplication by 3303 at the end of the inverse.
- The block holds the 256 coefficients itself. I load them over the shell while the block is idle, two coefficients to a shell write, ask for a forward or an inverse transform with a start command, and read the 256 results back
  over the shell, two to a read, once the block says it is done. The transform replaces the coefficients (in place).
- The block must raise a "busy" signal while it works and a "done" flag at the end. A new request will not come while it is busy.
- Time limit: from the clock that takes the start request to the clock before the "done" pulse it must take no more than 1,200 clocks for either direction, and I can read back how many clocks the last transform took.
  Use no divide operators and no remainder operators (they do not belong in a design for this part), and no floating-point blocks.
- CPU_RESETN clears busy and done. I will check several transforms exactly: forward ones (a single one, all coefficients 3328, a random one) and an inverse (on a random polynomial).
  LED0 shows done and LED1 shows busy. The shell runs at 115200 baud on the USB-UART. The design ID is "NTTE".

Test hooks: top module `c16_ntt_engine_top`, ports named as in the board's master XDC, and the test shell's
`CLKS_PER_BIT`, `TIMEOUT_CYCLES` and `BUILD_STAMP` parameters as top-level parameters. There are no other time
constants.

what: An engine for the number-theoretic transform used in the post-quantum key-exchange standard ML-KEM. It holds a polynomial of many coefficients, and transforms it forwards or backwards in place, with all arithmetic modulo a small prime. It avoids divide and remainder operators, stays within a clock limit and reports how long each transform took.
where: The transform makes polynomial multiplication fast in lattice-based cryptography, and is the heaviest step in post-quantum key exchange and signature schemes. Hardware engines speed it up for servers and embedded devices.
